title: Pakistan Army IBO in Barkhan Kills 7 'Indian-Backed' Fitna al-Hindustan Militants — Major Among 5 Soldiers Martyred
detail: Troops of the Pakistan Army and Frontier Corps Balochistan conducted an area sanitization operation in the Nosham area of Barkhan District, Balochistan on May 13, 2026. ISPR stated the targets were members of 'Fitna al-Hindustan' — Pakistan's military umbrella label for militant groups it attributes to Indian sponsorship operating across Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Seven militants were killed in firefighting; five Pakistani security personnel were martyred: Major Tauseef Ahmed Bhatti (31), Naik Fida Hussain (36), Sepoy Zakir Hussain (32), Sepoy Suhail Ahmed (21), and Sepoy Muhammad Ayaz (24). Weapons, ammunition, and explosives were recovered. DG ISPR Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry released a statement on X explicitly attributing the militants to 'Indian-backed' foreign sponsorship. Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi issued condolences for the fallen soldiers. The operation is part of Pakistan's ongoing 'Azm-e-Istehkam' counter-terrorism campaign. India has denied any involvement in Balochistan militancy; New Delhi characterizes ISPR's 'Fitna al-Hindustan' framing as a fabricated narrative used to justify domestic repression and shift international blame.

media.caption: Pakistan Army IBO in Barkhan: 7 Fitna al-Hindustan militants killed, 5 soldiers including a Major martyred on May 13, 2026

title: India Hosts BRICS Foreign Ministers' Summit in New Delhi — Jaishankar Chairs; Iran-UAE Crisis Dominates; No India-Pakistan Bilateral
detail: India chaired the BRICS Foreign Ministers' Summit at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on May 13–15, 2026, with External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar presiding. The two-day ministerial meeting — convening Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa and expanded BRICS+ members — was dominated by the Iran-UAE dispute and the broader US-Israel-Iran conflict situation, which overshadowed other agenda items. Pakistan is not a BRICS member; no India-Pakistan bilateral meeting took place on the sidelines. EAM Jaishankar held bilateral meetings with South Africa's Foreign Minister Ronald Lamola and Maldives FM Iruthisham Adam, among others. India's consistent diplomatic position — that bilateral talks with Pakistan are contingent on Islamabad dismantling cross-border terrorist infrastructure — remains fully in place. The summit underscored India's continued international diplomatic engagement and its role as a key multilateral convener, even as the bilateral relationship with Pakistan remains frozen across all channels. China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi also attended; China and India held a brief sideline exchange but no breakthrough on either the China-India border dossier or the India-Pakistan mediation track was reported.

media.caption: India hosts BRICS Foreign Ministers Summit in New Delhi, May 13–15, 2026 — EAM Jaishankar chairs as Iran-UAE crisis dominates agenda
